scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

M-ESTIMATED-DISPUTE-SHARE.name: Share of disputed bills carrying an ESTIMATED read type

M-DISPUTE-RESPONSE-P90.name: p90 dispute ticket response time vs SLA

F-01.statement: Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over period 2026-08..09, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL (3025 total).

F-03.statement: CRM dispute ticket response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-04.statement: Billing-db tariff_change_log contains 0 records: no tariff changes logged.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request field route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: Of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 are AMI-channel reads received before cutoff and exported but rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; 56 are AMI-channel with no read received before cutoff and not exported.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem, best solved by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets, as the requester's initial_request implies.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August (logged in DA-RULES) is causing bills to be computed or validated incorrectly, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI reads from the vendor-run MDMS (H-MDMS-BILL nightly export) are failing to deliver or are semantically invalid, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter reads from contracted field services (H-FIELD-BILL daily upload) are missing, late, or inaccurate, leading to estimate substitution and incorrect bills on manually-read accounts.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LOGIC.statement: The billing system's estimate-substitution step (used when no accepted read exists) is itself producing systematically wrong bills, independent of which upstream read source is missing.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL.statement: A field reader headcount shortfall since July (claimed by SH-FIELD) is the specific driver of the route completion shortfall seen in E-01, feeding estimate substitution and disputes.

H-BILLING-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJ.statement: Billing import rejects AMI reads flagged with high consumption (billing_import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution on otherwise-valid AMI reads, and this accounts for the large majority (1184 of 1240) of ESTIMATED-read disputed bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts (9200 accounts) was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, meaning roughly 7 percentage points of manual meter-read routes were not completed in the dispute-surge period, which the meter-to-cash process routes into estimate substitution when no accepted read exists.

The measured 88% manual-read route completion against a 95% target (9200 accounts, Aug-Sep 2026) still holds as a fact, but it no longer explains the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills: E-10 shows those bills are entirely AMI-channel records, not manual-read accounts, so route lateness/staffing does not feed this estimate-substitution pathway.

Of disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read and 1240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read, so a majority of disputes occur on bills that had an accepted meter read, not on estimate-substituted bills. This means theories tying the surge mainly to missing/failed reads feeding estimate substitution (AMI delivery, field-read handoff, or the estimate-substitution step itself) can at best explain the ESTIMATED subset and leave the larger ACTUAL-read share unexplained.

The 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL disputed-bill split still holds and still shows the majority of disputes carry an ACTUAL read, unexplained by any estimate-substitution theory; E-10 further shows the ESTIMATED subset itself is entirely AMI-channel and dominated by billing-import high-consumption rejections, so field-read-handoff/staffing-lateness is no longer a viable explanation even for that minority subset.

CRM response-time stats (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, SLA 3.0d, 2440 tickets) show dispute tickets are being answered within SLA on aggregate, so the surge is not explained by slow/inadequate ticket response — undercutting the premise that an auto-answering AI agent addresses the surge's cause.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff changes are logged in that system, which rules out a tariff/pricing change as a cause of the wrong bills or dispute surge.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly (E-05) shows monthly dispute counts of 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09): volume roughly doubles from the Jun-Jul baseline (~600/mo) to the Aug-Sep period (~1200/mo), confirming the surge's magnitude and August onset timing but saying nothing about its cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that there has been no tariff change this year is a stakeholder claim, non-authoritative, that corroborates the already-recorded tool finding (E-04: billing-db tariff_change_log has 0 records) rather than adding new authoritative information.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims field reading has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late, which pushes affected customers onto estimated bills. This is an uncorroborated stakeholder claim giving a specific causal mechanism (staffing) for route lateness, directionally consistent with E-01's 88% completion finding but not itself an authoritative measurement of staffing levels or causation.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) establishes that the utility may request field dispatch route priority changes but they are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation; this corroborates the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement for push_route_update as a contractual obligation held by SH-FIELD, not an internal policy choice.

E-09.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471). This is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that the access-pending blocker on mdms-export may now be lifted, but it does not itself confirm successful data retrieval or AMI read-event content.

E-10 breaks down the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (matching E-02's total exactly) and shows they are entirely AMI read-channel records: 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 (4.5%) had no AMI read received at all. This points to billing-import rejection of valid AMI reads flagged for high consumption as the dominant driver of estimate substitution for this subset, not missing manual field reads from route-completion/staffing lateness.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What causes the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of disputes), since the estimate-substitution/route-completion mechanism does not apply to bills with an accepted actual read?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether a billing import/validation rule change (DA-RULES) or another mechanism must be investigated before any remediation can address the majority of disputes.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query billing-config's billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes around August 2026 and cross-reference against ACTUAL-read disputed bills.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Limit any proposed fix to the ESTIMATED-read subset until the ACTUAL-read cause is established; do not claim coverage of the full dispute surge.

U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the claimed field-reader staffing shortfall (SH-FIELD, E-07) the actual driver of the route-completion shortfall in E-01, or is some other factor responsible?
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Affects whether any eventual remediation should target staffing/contract levels versus a different field-operations fix, given SH-FIELD's incentive bias toward headcount increase.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Obtain authoritative field-staffing/headcount records from ORG-FIELD and compare against the route completion timeline, independent of SH-FIELD's self-report.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the staffing shortfall as an unconfirmed contributing factor; do not propose dispatch/staffing changes based on this claim alone.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution: E-10 shows the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills are entirely AMI-channel records, of which 95.5% (1184) involve a received-but-rejected (HIGH_CONSUMPTION) AMI read rather than a missing manual read; this undercuts the staffing/route-completion pathway as the dominant explanation for ESTIMATED-read disputes, pointing instead to billing-import rejection logic.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-AVAILABILITY.question: Can authoritative AMI read-event data (DA-MDMS) be obtained to verify or further rule out AMI-related contributions, given mdms-export is DEGRADED and a non-transient ACCESS_PENDING hold was recorded?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-AVAILABILITY.decision_impact: Without MDMS access, AMI-side causes for the unexplained ACTUAL-read dispute majority cannot be directly tested, limiting confidence in fully excluding AMI issues.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-AVAILABILITY.resolution_path: Escalate vendor (ORG-AMI) provisioning of mdms-export access and retry once ACCESS_PENDING clears.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-AVAILABILITY.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-db, crm-tickets, route-log, and billing-config investigation without MDMS data in the interim.

U-BASELINE-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Review dispute volume trend further back than June 2026 if additional CRM history is available.
U-BASELINE-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Use the Jun-Jul 2026 average (E-05) as a provisional baseline target pending longer-history confirmation.

A-ESTIMATED-SUBSET-OVERLAP.statement: The 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-02) substantially correspond to the manual-read accounts whose routes under-completed in E-01, rather than a separate pathway.

A-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE.statement: SH-FIELD's self-reported 3-reader staffing shortage since July (E-07) is the actual cause of the route-completion shortfall, despite SH-FIELD's incentive to argue for headcount increase.
